extract.letter_transcript:
SUNRISE HEALTH PLAN
Sunrise Senior Advantage (HMO) - a Medicare Advantage plan
P.O. Box 4410, Oakland, CA 94612

NOTICE OF DENIAL OF MEDICAL COVERAGE

Date of notice: October 6, 2026

Member: Maria Delgado
Member ID: SSA-88214077
Requesting provider: Dr. Priya Raman, MD - Bayview Endocrine Associates

Service requested: Continuous glucose monitor (Dexcom G7) with supplies
HCPCS: E2103 Non-adjunctive CGM receiver; A4239 Supply allowance for non-adjunctive CGM, 1 month
Diagnosis: E11.649 Type 2 diabetes mellitus with hypoglycemia without coma; Z79.4 Long term (current) use of insulin
Requested date of service: September 29, 2026
Amount: $1,284.00

We have denied your request for the service listed above.

Why we denied your request:
The requested continuous glucose monitor is not medically necessary. The member does not meet coverage criteria because the member is not performing blood glucose testing four or more times per day, and the member is not insulin-treated with multiple (three or more) daily administrations of insulin or a continuous subcutaneous insulin infusion pump. Per plan clinical guidelines, a CGM is covered only for members on intensive insulin therapy.

This decision was made by the Sunrise Health Plan Utilization Management department.

You have the right to ask Sunrise Senior Advantage to reconsider this decision. You must ask for a reconsideration within 65 calendar days from the date of this notice. If you or your doctor believe that waiting for a standard decision could seriously harm your health, you can ask for a fast (expedited) decision.

match.summary: The denial is inconsistent with the effective LCD L33822 ("current") policy and the patient's chart because it relies on obsolete criteria (4+ daily BGM tests and 3+ daily insulin administrations or CSII pump) that were removed prior to the 2026-09-29 date of service. The chart documents that Maria Delgado meets all required initial coverage criteria under the effective policy—including Type 2 diabetes, CGM training and prescription per FDA indications, insulin treatment (c4a) as well as a level 3 hypoglycemic event (c4b2), and an in-person evaluation within 6 months prior to ordering—so the denial should be overturned.

letter:
On behalf of Maria Delgado (Member ID: SSA-88214077), we respectfully request reconsideration of Sunrise Senior Advantage (HMO)'s October 6, 2026 denial of a continuous glucose monitor (Dexcom G7) with supplies (HCPCS E2103, A4239; ICD-10 E11.649, Z79.4) for date of service September 29, 2026. The plan denied the request as not medically necessary, asserting that the patient does not perform blood glucose testing four or more times per day, is not treated with three or more daily insulin administrations or an insulin pump, and is not on intensive insulin therapy.

## Governing coverage criteria

Under 42 CFR § 422.101(b)(1), (b)(3), and (b)(6), Medicare Advantage organizations must comply with Traditional Medicare coverage criteria when fully established in Local Coverage Determinations (LCDs) and may not apply more restrictive internal guidelines. The governing policy for date of service September 29, 2026 is LCD L33822 (Glucose Monitors), version effective October 1, 2024. The requirements cited in the denial notice are not part of this effective policy: CMS removed the requirement to test blood glucose four or more times daily on July 18, 2021, and removed the requirement for three or more daily insulin administrations or an insulin pump on April 16, 2023. Furthermore, the plan's restriction limiting coverage to members on intensive insulin therapy does not appear in any version of L33822.

## The patient meets each criterion

The medical record demonstrates that Ms. Delgado satisfies every criterion of L33822 (effective October 1, 2024):

- **Diabetes mellitus diagnosis:** [[Q:r1:policy]] The 09/15/2026 office visit documents Type 2 diabetes mellitus (ICD-10 E11.649), noted in her history since 2011: [[Q:r1:chart]]
- **Training and prescription:** [[Q:r2:policy]] Dr. Priya Raman documented CGM alert training for the patient and her husband on 09/15/2026 and prescribed the Dexcom G7 on 09/22/2026: [[Q:r2:chart]]
- **Prescribed per FDA indications:** [[Q:r3:policy]] The 09/15/2026 treatment plan specifies non-adjunctive use in accordance with FDA indications: [[Q:r3:chart]]
- **Insulin-treated:** [[Q:r4:policy]] The patient is treated with once-daily subcutaneous insulin glargine (22 units at bedtime), satisfying the insulin treatment requirement: [[Q:r4:chart]]
- **Level 3 hypoglycemic event:** [[Q:r5:policy]] The 08/30/2026 emergency department summary documents a glucose of 41 mg/dL with confusion and unresponsiveness requiring 911 activation and paramedic IV dextrose: [[Q:r5:chart]]
- **Recent in-person visit:** [[Q:r6:policy]] Dr. Priya Raman conducted an in-person evaluation on 09/15/2026, seven days before the 09/22/2026 order: [[Q:r6:chart]]

## Procedural issues

In addition to relying on retired and unauthorized criteria in violation of 42 CFR § 422.101(b)(3) and (b)(6), the October 6, 2026 denial notice fails to identify the specific coverage policy or criterion relied upon, as required by 42 CFR § 422.568(e) and CMS-0057-F. The notice also omits the reviewing clinician's identity and specialty, which is required to confirm appropriate expertise under 42 CFR § 422.566(d).

## Request

Because Ms. Delgado meets all six criteria of the governing LCD L33822, we request that Sunrise Senior Advantage (HMO) overturn this denial and authorize coverage for HCPCS E2103 and A4239 for date of service September 29, 2026. If the denial is upheld at any stage, please provide the name and clinical specialty of the reviewing professional pursuant to 42 CFR § 422.566(d).

explain.English:
Hi Maria,

We are writing to update you about your Dexcom G7 continuous glucose monitor. Your health plan denied coverage, but we believe their decision is wrong. 

They based their denial on old rules that are no longer active, like needing four daily finger sticks or three daily insulin shots. Under the official current policy, called LCD L33822, you fully qualify for the monitor. Your medical records show you meet all six required criteria, including your Type 2 diabetes, your insulin use, a severe low blood sugar event, and your recent doctor visit within six months.

Our care team is already appealing this denial to get it overturned before the December 10, 2026 deadline. You also have the right to call your insurance plan and ask for the credentials of the person who reviewed your request. We are right here to support you!
explain.Spanish:
Hola María. Queremos informarle que su seguro rechazó la cobertura de su monitor continuo de glucosa Dexcom G7. No se preocupe, nuestro equipo de atención médica ya está preparando una apelación para defender su caso.

La negativa del seguro se basa en requisitos antiguos que ya fueron retirados, como exigir cuatro pinchazos de dedo diarios o tres inyecciones de insulina. El plan debe seguir la norma vigente L33822 y no citó una política de cobertura específica para negar el servicio. Su expediente médico demuestra que usted cumple con todos los requisitos actuales: tiene diabetes tipo 2, usa tratamiento de insulina, tuvo un episodio grave de bajo azúcar en sangre y asistió a sus citas médicas.

La fecha límite para presentar la apelación es el 10 de diciembre de 2026. Además, usted tiene derecho a llamar a su seguro para solicitar las credenciales médicas del revisor que tomó esta decisión. Estamos aquí para apoyarla en todo este proceso.

objections.objection: The plan requires multiple daily insulin injections (MDI) or an insulin pump rather than just once-daily basal insulin for CGM coverage.
objections.response: Under the effective governing policy (LCD L33822), the criteria requires any insulin regimen, not exclusively MDI or pump therapy. The denial relies on a retired requirement or unapproved internal plan criteria in violation of 42 CFR § 422.101(b). The patient meets the insulin requirement with her daily subcutaneous insulin glargine regimen.

objections.objection: The patient does not have a documented history of recurrent severe hypoglycemia or frequent blood glucose testing logs.
objections.response: The governing policy requires a qualifying hypoglycemic event; the patient's records confirm a Level 3 hypoglycemic event (POC glucose 41 mg/dL) resulting in confusion and unresponsiveness, which required 911 activation and paramedic IV dextrose administration. Applying unstated or retired criteria violates 42 CFR § 422.101(b).

objections.objection: There is insufficient documentation demonstrating proper training, FDA-aligned prescribing, or recent clinical evaluation for CGM initiation.
objections.response: All clinical documentation requirements are fully met: Dr. Raman evaluated the patient in-person on 09/15/2026, documented a Type 2 diabetes diagnosis, prescribed the Dexcom G7 per FDA indications on 09/22/2026, and trained the patient and her husband on CGM alerts.
